# Honest titles for reproduction "signed" prints

**13,538 poster and print listings** describe a printed signature as "Signed" or "Autographed". These files rename them so the title says what the customer gets. Generated by `tools/signed_titles.py`:

- removes the product type pasted at the start of the title ("Signed Footballer Posters …");
- "Signed / Autographed / Signed Autographed" → **"Printed Signature"**;
- "Merch / Memorabilia" → "Gift";
- adds **"– Reproduction Print"** at the end.

Example: `Signed Music Posters Stevie Wonder 1 - Signed Autographed Music Star Print` → `Stevie Wonder 1 - Printed Signature Music Star Print – Reproduction Print`.

Left alone: Sport Cards (44) and custom bricks (19), which aren't prints. Handles (URLs) don't change, so links and Google history are kept.

`before-after-review.csv` lists every old and new title so you can check them.

## Import
1. Products → Import → `00-TEST-3-products.csv`, with **"Overwrite products with matching handles"** ticked.
2. Check those 3 products: only the title should change.
3. Then import `01-signed-titles.csv` and `02-signed-titles.csv`.

The Foxy Pop theme also shows a "printed reproduction, not hand-signed" notice on every one of these product pages automatically.

> Some titles also say "Limited Edition". Keep that only if the prints really are limited runs. Tell Claude and those words can be removed too.
